security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI M-mode firmware configures PMP/ePMP entries during domain protection setup (sbi_hart_oldpmp_configure / sbi_hart_smepmp_configure) that deny execute permission from S/U-mode to memory regions containing shared vector tables, when CLIC-style xivt/xeivt (or analogous mivt/meivt) CSRs are programmed to share a single vector table across M-mode and S-mode.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: PMP entry with L=1 and X=0 (or Smepmp locked-shared-code with X=0) whose address range covers the vector table base in a system where xivt/xeivt enables cross-privilege vector-table sharing; also: domain memory regions that omit the vector table page entirely from the S-mode domain's allowed-PMP set.
security_spec.summary: OpenSBI PMP configuration must grant execute permission to S/U-mode for shared vector table regions when CLIC-style xivt/xeivt sharing is enabled, or S-mode interrupt delivery fails due to PMP execute faults.

findings.finding: Root domain firmware regions are configured as M-only (no SU_READABLE/SU_EXECUTABLE bits), and the catch-all SU RWX region only covers addresses NOT matched by firmware entries. If a CLIC-style shared vector table (mivt/meivt/xivt/xeivt) resides in firmware address space, S-mode will be denied all access because PMP entry priority causes the M-only firmware entry to match first, blocking the SU catch-all. This would cause denial-of-service when CLIC hardware shares the vector table page across privilege modes.

Old PMP configure iterates domain regions and programs PMP entries via pmp_set() in index-priority order. Firmware regions (M-only) come first in the sorted region list and will match before the SU catch-all. If a shared vector table page falls within a firmware region's address range, S/U-mode execute/read is denied with no recovery path. The function has no awareness of CLIC-style vector table sharing and provides no mechanism to carve out an exception for the shared vector table page.

Smepmp configure uses a two-pass approach (M-only regions with MML=0, then shared/SU regions with MML=1). Firmware regions are tracked in fw_smepmp_ids bitmap and preserved across domain switches. Under Smepmp, M-mode only gets explicit access to listed regions, making the separation even stricter than old PMP. If a CLIC shared vector table is in firmware memory, S-mode has no entry covering it — the M-only firmware entry matches first. No carve-out mechanism exists for shared vector table pages that need cross-privilege access.

Flag translation correctly maps SBI_DOMAIN_MEMREGION_SU_EXECUTABLE to PMP_X. For regions without SU_EXECUTABLE, PMP_X is not set, correctly denying execute. This function itself is correct — the risk lies in domain region definitions, not the flag translation.

Smepmp flag translation correctly maps shared-region types to Smepmp encoding. For SURW_MRW (shared read/write), the encoding is PMP_W|PMP_X which under MML=1 grants SU R/W without execute — correct deny-execute behavior. For SUR_MR (shared read-only), encoding PMP_L|PMP_R|PMP_W|PMP_X grants SU read-only. No encoding error here.

EIC770x custom PMP configure skips firmware regions entirely (line 296-297), meaning the shared vector table page — if it overlaps firmware memory — gets no PMP entry at all. Subsequent non-firmware regions are programmed with oldpmp flags, and unused slots are disabled. In the gap between firmware entries (configured in early_init) and the skipped firmware regions, the PMP default-deny behavior denies all S/U-mode access. No explicit handling for shared vector table carve-out.

Domain context switch correctly unconfigures old PMP and configures new PMP for the target domain. The unconfigure path (sbi_hart_pmp_unconfigure) preserves Smepmp firmware entries. No stale-PMP risk across domain switches.
